newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin names liberal Nemtsov energy minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin names liberal Nemtsov energy minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has appointed First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov as Russia's new fuel and energy minister, the Kremlin said on Thursday.
The move appeared aimed at speeding up market reforms in a stragetic sector of Russia's economy.

Nemtsov, a youthful liberal, was only drafted into the cabinet last month as part of a wide-ranging government reshuffle to oversee the restructuring of natural monopolies like gas, electricity and railways and housing reform.
Nemtsov, 37, is one of Russia's most popular politicians and is seen as a possible successor to Yeltsin after the president retires in the year 2000.

In a radio address to the nation earlier on Thursday Yeltsin, 66, said he wanted to put more younger people in positions of responsibility, saying they were the best guarantee of Russia's economic reforms.
Earlier this week, during a tour of the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk, Nemtsov himself called for young people to take a lead in Russian politics and industry.
Nemtsov has praised Yeltsin regularly and refers to him as a kind tsar in a new book.

Until his promotion to the government, Nemtsov was governor of the car-making city of Nizhny Novgorod and its surrounding region, 400 km (250 miles) east of Moscow, where he pioneered privatisation and other market reforms.

Born in the Black Sea resort of Sochi, Nemtsov graduated in radio physics from Gorky University in 1981 and worked as an engineer in the city. He took his first steps in politics during the Soviet era as an environmental campaigner.
Yeltsin appointed him head of the Nizhny Novgorod administration in November 1991 as the Soviet Union broke up, giving him a seat in the Russian Federation Council's upper house.
He was elected in December 1995 and returned, comfortably, last autumn.
